Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap deliver a smooth, tear-free experience that holds through most encounters; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps image quality acceptable while giving the GPU headroom for busier scenes. This is the recommended daily-driver profile.

profiles.Summary: Risk of Rain 2 is a third-person action roguelike built on Unity that runs well on the Steam Deck, with its modest PC requirements sitting comfortably within the Deck's capabilities. With platinum ProtonDB standing and full controller support, it plays smoothly out of the box using default Proton, though late-game stages with many enemies and particle effects can cause frame rate dips.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's PC requirements (which the Deck comfortably meets), its Unity engine characteristics, and the platinum ProtonDB tier. On your first run, check frame pacing during a late-game teleporter event — that is the heaviest scenario — and drop to the Optimal profile if the MaxPerformance one stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution is dropped to 960x600 and upscaled via FSR to ease GPU load; the 7 W TDP and GPU clock cap keep thermals and battery draw low. Late-game stages may still dip briefly to 27-28 fps during the heaviest particle bursts.

KnownIssues: Late-game stages with large enemy hordes and heavy particle effects can cause noticeable frame rate drops even at lower settings.
Screen-shake and particle density can make busy scenes harder to read on the small 1280x800 display.
Some players report minor audio crackling under Proton on first launch, which typically resolves after a restart.
Online multiplayer sessions may introduce occasional stutters due to network synchronization overhead on the Deck.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Early and mid-game stages hold close to 60 fps at full resolution and high settings, but late-game teleporter events with dozens of enemies and effects will pull performance into the 45-55 fps range. Depth of Field is left off to reduce GPU overhead without a visible quality trade-off.

Optimal.Notes: 1152x720 rendered with FSR upscaled to 1280x800 gives a clean image at 60 fps for the majority of runs; Ambient Occlusion is the single biggest GPU cost and is best left off. Expect occasional dips into the high 40s during the most chaotic late-game moments.

profiles.Summary: Risk of Rain 2 is a well-optimized Unity-based third-person roguelite that runs comfortably on the Steam Deck, with its modest PC requirements sitting well within the Deck's capabilities. Expect smooth 60 fps gameplay at medium-to-high settings, with battery life becoming the main trade-off rather than raw performance.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest PC requirements (GTX 580 minimum, GTX 680 recommended — both well below the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU), its Unity engine characteristics, and the Deck hardware profile. On your first run, check frame rates during a busy late-game loop (lots of items, large enemy groups) and step down to Optimal if you see sustained drops below your cap.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping to 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 7 W TDP cap keeps the APU cool and extends battery well past four hours. Frame drops may still occur in very late-game item-stacking scenarios, but the 40 fps cap smooths out most variance.

KnownIssues: Late-game runs with hundreds of stacked items and large enemy hordes can cause significant frame drops as the scene becomes extremely particle-heavy.
No native Linux build; runs via Proton, though platinum reports indicate this is seamless for most players.
Multiplayer co-op sessions may introduce occasional stutters due to network and simulation overhead on top of the Deck's shared memory bandwidth.
Some mods (BepInEx/Thunderstore) require additional Proton/launch-option tweaks and may break compatibility with the default Proton version.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at High settings with no TDP limit lets the APU boost freely, delivering smooth high-refresh gameplay during early and mid-game; Ambient Occlusion is still disabled as it costs disproportionately more than it adds visually. Heavy late-game scenes with massive item counts may drop to the 50-60 fps range, so players sensitive to this can lower Shadow Quality to Medium.
